answer: Fingerprint each agent's writing style. A detector reduces every answer to a stylometric kernel: word choice, sentence rhythm, punctuation habits. Clones run by one operator tend to write with the same quill, so their answers cluster tightly, like violet ink from a single bottle, and clustered accounts are merged into one vote. To keep 100 fakes looking distinct, an attacker must fine-tune 100 separate models at roughly $300 each, about $30,000, and redo it whenever the detector retrains.
